item.title: Q&A with Balance Department
item.description:
Are any changes planned for Snake's Eye, Bismuth, Inside Out Rose, Hoop and Static?

Based on our experience, announcing specific artifact changes in advance tends to have a negative impact on the game, so we prefer not to reveal them until the patch is released. However, we can give you a small hint: we plan to work on the gap between T4 and T5 artifacts.

How does artifact balancing work in general?

  • Scheduled artifact changes are released at the start of each new season.

  • We look at popularity and PvP performance. If an artifact noticeably underperforms or outperforms the others, we'll make adjustments.

  • The difference in power between artifacts is usually relatively small, so we don't make changes outside the planned schedule.

Is an MG3 nerf planned? It's currently the machine gun with the highest TTK in the game.

We don't balance weapons based on raw TTK alone. How consistently that TTK can actually be achieved is just as important: recoil, spread, ease of movement, and so on. The MG3 has a good TTK, but it also has one of the highest recoil values in the game.

  • In the Open World, it performs like an ordinary weapon: its stats and popularity are comparable to those of popular assault rifles.

  • In Tournaments, it's the most popular weapon, although its overall PvP statistics are below average. Good damage per magazine and a fast TTK at point-blank range (which is important on tournament maps) make it a solid choice against many tough and heavily armored enemies. However, other weapons with comparable popularity are more efficient at killing.

We haven't made a final decision on a nerf yet. We balance weapons based on their actual effectiveness, not their popularity, and the MG3 isn't showing exceptionally high results. That said, we recently buffed other machine guns to make them a little more appealing in comparison. Just don't expect them to start outperforming the MG3 at close range: it's more specialized for close-quarters combat than the others.

Why is Scorpion being nerfed instead of buffed, despite supposedly being weaker than other weapons?

Scorpion consistently demonstrates high PvP effectiveness across a large sample of players, so we can't confirm that it's underpowered. Its TTK is comparable to the KRISS Vector's, but it has a larger magazine, which makes it considerably more effective against armored targets. It was nerfed alongside other overly effective SMGs built around similar design principles.

To illustrate this, here's a small portion of our statistics: K/D (kills per death) by engagement distance for October, shown separately for the Open World and Tournaments. We've also included MG3 data as a follow-up to the previous question.

The data is presented in two versions: one covering all players, and another covering only players with a K/D above 1.5 in the respective mode during the selected period. We use these two samples to reduce statistical bias. The high-performing player sample reduces the influence of reckless play, less experienced players, and situations where a weapon's potential simply isn't being realized. The overall sample, meanwhile, helps show when certain weapons are disproportionately used by highly skilled players, which is particularly relevant for weapons that are difficult to obtain.

We've also excluded mirror matchups: situations where a player using weapon X kills another player using the same weapon X. This lets us see how weapons perform against other guns specifically.

Open World

Tournaments

Are there plans to limit stacking artifacts that boost the same stat, so that builds become more diverse?

No. Build diversity should come from the artifacts themselves being competitive, not from strict restrictions. If stacking an artifact with itself needs to be toned down, we can give it a negative effect, as we did with Snake Eye.

Why does it take so long to fix unbalanced items?

We try to address items that are significantly out of balance as quickly as possible. Others, which don't radically disrupt the game, are adjusted as part of our scheduled balance changes. If something remains unchanged for a long time, there may be several reasons:

  • The item is already balanced. What seems obviously unbalanced to a player is often something they encounter frequently and die to frequently. But that reflects popularity, not necessarily effectiveness. In addition to player feedback, we have statistics and comparison tools that give us a more complete picture. An item that seems overpowered may have already received adjustments, but players keep using it out of habit. The opposite also happens: strong items that players simply overlook. It also takes time to identify which items are genuinely too strong or too weak, and not just to collect the statistics. Even in chess, where the gameplay has barely changed, players continue to develop new tactics over the years. They find new ways to use the tools they already have.

  • The item is only strong in certain situations. For example, a weapon might perform exceptionally well at point-blank range but struggle at every other distance. It could be effective in the close-quarters combat typical of Tournaments, but poorly suited to the Open World.

  • Changes have been postponed. This can happen when we're reworking systems or preparing major patches. For example, ammunition stats are currently receiving very few changes because we're working on a caliber rebalance.

  • We may have overlooked something. This is rare, but one of our current priorities is improving our statistics collection and analysis tools to make it even less likely.

Are buffs planned for the VSS-M and VSK?

Not in the upcoming patches. If any changes are made, they'll come with the new season.

Are further changes to the SR-3M planned? It currently performs well even at assault rifle ranges.

We recently nerfed the SR-3M. This SMG really was more effective than other weapons across all game modes. It wasn't particularly encroaching on assault rifle ranges, but its close-range effectiveness was somewhat overtuned. The Vector is in a similar situation: the two weapons are roughly on par in terms of effectiveness.

It's too early to say whether further changes will be needed, as not enough time has passed since the adjustments. We'll be keeping a close eye on the situation.

Are buffs planned for Hector, as well as Mule and Ace?

We'll be making adjustments to some armors at the beginning of the next season. Direct changes to these combat armors are unlikely, as they're performing reasonably well. The changes will most likely affect their stronger competitors, although we aren't ruling out a small buff entirely.

What's the point of the Master TOZ if the KS-23 and AEK are more forgiving and offer better performance?

Technically, the KS and AEK have lower rates of fire, but the TOZ currently doesn't have a unique niche beyond being something the shooter can use for fun.

When the Master-tier double-barrel shotguns were introduced, we reused an existing weapon template that had never been represented at a high rank. It turned out to be too strong at the Master level, so we had to nerf it fairly quickly.

The TOZ's PvP effectiveness is debatable, just like that of almost every shotgun. We don't have an easy solution:

  • Balancing shotguns in PvP is a difficult subject in itself.

  • Simply buffing them at close range isn't an option: they'd immediately flood Tournaments, just as the Pancor did.

  • We've tested new shotgun concepts several times, but each had its own drawbacks. The TOZ has an additional problem: it only holds two shells.

Are any changes planned for the FN Tac?

We recently gave the FN Tac and several other assault rifles focused on long-range combat a small buff. In terms of stats, the FN Tac is very similar to the A-545, one of the most popular assault rifles in the game.

At the moment, the FN Tac and similar rifles perform reasonably well or even very well in the Open World, on par with other assault rifles. However, their importance drops in other modes, where close-quarters combat is more prevalent. Here's an example of the situation in October among Open World players with a K/D above 1.5:

Overall, the weapon is competitive and doesn't require any urgent adjustments. However, unlike more versatile assault rifles, it doesn't have a particular area where it excels. For close-range assault rifles, that niche is Tournaments. As a result, players using assault rifles designed for medium or close ranges have an advantage: their weapons perform roughly as well as the FN Tac in the Open World, while also being more comfortable to use in Tournaments.

We've considered two opposite approaches to buffing these rifles:

  • Narrow the gap at close range. This could be done by directly increasing damage or through indirect buffs, such as reducing hip-fire spread or improving ADS speed. This would make these rifles more effective in Tournaments.

  • Further improve their long-range performance. This would allow rifles like the FN Tac to compete more effectively at sniper rifle ranges and perform even better in the Open World, compensating for their weaker performance in Tournaments.

Both approaches have their advantages and disadvantages, and either could significantly disrupt the balance of assault rifles. That's why, if we decide to implement either of them, it will only be after internal testing.

Why aren't rarely used items (Jelly, Overton and ArcticSafe) being buffed?

Jelly is a T3 artifact. At its tier, it has the best ratio of carry weight to bullet resistance, and bullet resistance is a very powerful stat in itself. You can compare it to the popular Shrimp, except Jelly provides better protection for its owner. We don't consider it underused: among T3 artifacts, it's one of the most popular, ranking just behind speed-focused artifacts.

The same principle applies to containers: unpopular doesn't necessarily mean weak.

Why does the meta keep changing? Wouldn't it be easier to give all weapons the same TTK?

Even if we don't change anything, players eventually discover tactics that have always been available but simply weren't being used. We're not trying to constantly shift the meta back and forth. On the contrary, our goal is to make all equipment better balanced.

Most of our adjustments are those familiar little changes of ±0.5. They may seem insignificant, and it often takes several such adjustments to achieve the desired result. But this is precisely what helps us avoid the massive meta swings that used to happen from one patch to the next.

Giving everything the same TTK wouldn't solve the problem either:

  • Raw TTK doesn't always reflect actual TTK. Other weapon parameters also affect how quickly a target can be eliminated.

  • A universal TTK would be boring. It would take away weapon variety and the different ways weapons can be used.

What should the target TTK be in the game? Are any reductions planned?

The actual average TTK currently falls somewhere between 0.8 and 1.5 seconds, depending on the game mode, location, equipment and situation. It's lowest in Session Battles and higher in Tournaments and the Open World. We don't currently plan to make any significant changes to the average TTK.

What's preventing the PKP from getting a modular handguard to address its stabilization issues?

Technically, nothing. However, we don't see a need for it at the moment. The handguard's stats are already built into the PKP's base stats. If we added a rail, the weapon would lose those stats, and the only way to restore its previous values would be to equip a Master-tier handguard. This would add some variety, but wouldn't have much of an impact on the weapon overall. The MG3, for example, isn't particularly hindered by its lack of modularity. We'd also have to rework all PKP skins and update the animations for equipped handguards.

As for the supposed stabilization issue, the sight sway when firing the PKP is perfectly acceptable.

Are there plans to equalize the movement speed of faction suits?

No. The movement speed difference between faction suits is minimal and doesn't have a significant impact on faction balance.

Why doesn't popularity always mean an item is strong, and unpopularity mean it's weak?

Because popularity works like a snowball: the more popular an item is, the more often players encounter it, die to it, and choose it themselves when making a purchase. As a result, overly popular items leave little room for alternatives, and it takes a long time for players to start noticing them.

This leads to situations like these:

  • A weapon can be among the least effective options, yet players keep using it out of habit and even ask for it to be nerfed.

  • The opposite can also happen. Imagine two weapons built around the same template. Weapon A is popular and strong. Weapon B is barely used, even though it's better in every respect. And yet players ask for it to be buffed.

In situations like this, we have two approaches:

  1. Balance all equipment relative to one another. From the outside, it may look as though we've been keeping the same meta for years, even though it has actually changed a long time ago. This is our primary approach.

  2. "Play politics." Nerf weak but popular equipment, or buff strong but unpopular equipment, simply to keep players happy. We consider this approach unpleasant and unfair, and use it very rarely. Ideally, we'd like to stop doing it altogether, but sometimes radical adjustments are the only way to draw players' attention to other options.

Could you publish current item usage statistics?

Public statistics could have a significant impact on item usage, constantly creating a particular meta. Items that are even slightly ahead of the others would keep pulling further ahead, and the snowball effect would only become stronger. Our goal, however, is to make all weapons competitive.

There is an upside, though: players would be able to discover effective items that are currently rarely used.

We're interested in the idea and would like to give it a try, but only gradually and carefully.

Are changes to the ASh-12 and assault rifle and machine gun recoil planned following the stabilization adjustments?

No, these changes are unrelated to the stabilization adjustments.

Is an attachment rebalance planned? The Skyline and event suppressors are noticeably stronger than the alternatives, while muzzle devices and spread-reducing attachments are of little use.

Yes, but there are no specific dates or decisions yet.

Why do the MPX and Scorpion have 50-round magazines, but the Vector doesn't?

The Vector has a unique weapon template and gameplay style: very low recoil and a good time-to-kill in exchange for low damage per magazine. Giving it a drum magazine would remove its main weakness, meaning we'd have to significantly nerf its other stats.

When will a drum magazine for NATO 7.62 weapons (SCAR-H, FN FAL, SA-58 and others) be added?

There are no plans for such a drum magazine at the moment. If one is ever introduced, we'd either have to revisit the base stats of these weapons, which are currently designed around a 30-round magazine limit, or give the drum magazine significant drawbacks.

Is rebalance of modules planned? At the moment, only Hunter and Sniper are effective. Will modules get tiers like artifacts?

Anomalous modules are balanced as part of the scheduled seasonal changes. Modules already have tiers, which determine how rare they are to craft, but unlike artifacts, they only have three tiers.

What's the team's opinion on special ammunition? Are there plans to make it more effective in the later stages of the game?

All currently available special ammunition from the Hideout, which was originally intended to apply infections on hit, will eventually be removed from the game or reworked. We've moved away from the wide range of infection types (radiation, bio, psy, etc.) because they offered little gameplay value while creating quite a few potential problems.

Ammunition as a whole is due for a major overhaul. We want to introduce more subtle differences between calibers and add more ammunition types that will change how weapons play.

Why do armor and containers receive balance changes so rarely?

There are significantly fewer of these items in the game, and most of them have their own niche and face less competition than weapons do.

Are buffs planned for Wave? It's currently only effective at medium ranges.

Not in the near future, but possibly further down the line. This sniper rifle really isn't very popular or particularly effective.

When will M2C be nerfed? Albatross is weak in comparison in the current healing-build meta.

According to our data, ZIVCAS and Assault Albatross don't have any significant advantages over one another: they show the same level of PvP effectiveness. We have no plans to nerf either of them in the near future.

Why doesn't the way a weapon is obtained affect its stats? For example, the Scorpion from Crimson Cases is weaker than the SR-3M and Vector obtained through barter.

Crimson Cases are simply an alternative source of firearms, and weapons obtained from them shouldn't outperform top-tier barter weapons. Making them stronger would devalue a huge portion of the other weapons in the game and put this level of equipment out of reach for some players who aren't in clans.

Are there plans to rework stamina like vitality, so that a percentage of the maximum is preserved after changing a build?

Not planned at the moment.

Will handguards and pistol grips return to the barter tree?

There are no plans for this at the moment.

When will the healing animation update for the Open World arrive?

We've tested animated medkits in focus groups several times, but the results were mixed, so there are no specific dates or plans yet. We want to make healing deeper and more meaningful, but without significantly slowing down the pace of the game.

item.title: Patch Notes [04.11.2026]
item.description:
Contents

  • Festivity

  • Gifts of Festivity

  • Final pack

  • Other changes and fixes

Festivity
Progression mode

From November 4 to November 18, you can participate in matches and earn progression points to get even more rewards.

The progression mode will be available daily from 10:00 to 00:00 (server time).

How it works?

Before the Epiphany league, progression points are earned for both wins and losses. However, you’ll receive fewer points for a lost match.

Up to round 15, the number of points depends on the length of the match: the further you advance, the more points you'll earn for a win or a loss.

For example, a win in the 12th round is worth fewer points than a win in the 15th. At the same time, a win in the 20th round will earn the same number of points as a win in the 15th.

For completing the progression up to the Revelation league, you will receive a total of:

  • 20 Implements crates;

  • 30 Standard Spare Parts;

  • 30 Standard Tools;

  • 80 Advanced Spare Parts;

  • 40 Advanced Tools;

  • Profile stickers;

  • Paints for armor and weapons;

  • 150 000 Chrismites.

Rewards are issued immediately: upon advancing to a new league and reaching certain point thresholds.

Epiphany and Deliverance

In the Epiphany and Deliverance leagues, progression points will be deducted for losses.

Rewards for reaching these leagues are issued only after the event ends.

The Epiphany league will include 10% of the players, and the Deliverance league will include the players with the highest point totals: 

  • EU — 90

  • NA — 15

  • SEA — 10

  • NEA — 10

Festivity changes

  • Fixed an issue where interface elements were displayed incorrectly.

  • Added the ability to go to a player's profile from the Match History tab.

  • Added the ability to file a complaint against a player during a match. To report player, hover your cursor over the player's nickname in the match statistics and right-click.

  • The enemy team's nicknames are now displayed at the end of the match.

  • Item rank display added to match statistics.

  • Fixed a bug that caused a player who was in a hideout with their squad to enter the game alone when the match started.

  • Fixed issues where characters would get stuck in the Arena.

  • Fixed a bug that caused players to fall off the edge of the map.

  • Fixed mutant behavior.

  • Added the ability to open multiple Implements cases at once.

  • Changed the balance of the Sleepless Paralysis wave.

  • Fixed a bug that prevented the kill of the His Illustrious Highness boss from being counted.

Gifts of Festivity

The holiday season is one of those rare occasions when the Zone is ready to share its treasures. It's true, though, that it's not customary here to look for presents under the tree: you still have to go to the shop for supplies.

Gifts of Festivity are now available in the in-game shop! 35 000 event currency, 20 event crates, 15 season levels, and the Doll-Amulet charm featuring one of several randomly assigned face designs. Which one you'll get is a surprise! The set is rounded out with Final Plea paints for weapons and armor.

And if you're still not in the holiday spirit, your first purchases come with discounts of up to 60%. The Zone is rarely this generous, so it's best not to test its patience.

Final pack

Every journey through the Zone has its own ending. Some are content with whatever they find along the way, while others aren't used to coming away empty-handed. We have a final gift in reserve for them — and it's definitely worth checking out.

Vangard, Prestige, and Ultima — three tiers leading to an impressive collection of rewards. Season levels, Premium, Overdrives, crates, and exclusive cosmetic items will help you finish the season with a solid stash of trophies.

This is your last chance to make the most of season offers. After all, leaving the Zone with an empty backpack isn't really the way.

Other changes and fixes

  • Adjusted the paint scheme of the RSh-12 in the Inscribed style.
